scope: D3D9 additional swap chains now use the existing supported render-target multisampling/resolve path, forwarding the requested sample type and validated quality to storage instead of refusing every nonzero type or silently creating NONE. Unsupported sample modes still fail before allocation/emission; cached parameters/Surface.GetDesc and capability quality-level metadata agree. Shared D3D8/9 SDK probes both construct 4x additional buffers, retain them through 32 public-zero chain revivals per API and present two exact colors, then perform binding-only Reset/private-object cleanup. Independent replay validates actual four-sample GPU attachment pixels through a separate explicit resolve, the host resolved texture and displayed scanout. Structural MSAA/flag/quality guards from 8b remain unchanged. Update the older manual MSAA SDK to expect the newly supported D3D9 additional case; the immutable 8b fixture preserves historical unsupported behavior. Full MSAA/format/depth compatibility, refresh/fullscreen validation, multiple-buffer storage/rotation, standalone target counts, complete Reset/thread/device loss, original Microsoft HAL, games/FPS and review stages 4/5/6 remain incomplete. No host/protocol/shader/bundle change.

sources.evidence: Pinned implementation AddRef from public zero acquires a parent device and physical swap-chain storage reference; Release to zero drops these references. Public surface references retain the same physical chain. This is implementation evidence for valid zero-count revival while storage survives, not a claim that repeated zero-count D3D8 chain Release is a native API guarantee.

Surface AddRef/Release maintain their own resource.refcount for non-texture public surfaces; device and underlying texture/swapchain references change only on public zero/nonzero edges. Release storage before the parent device, since storage destruction can free the surface.

Pinned Windows additional-chain test_refcount: backbuffer container is its IDirect3DSwapChain9; surface public count starts at one and has an independent device pin. Pinned swapchain implementation pins its parent only at public zero/nonzero edges.
Non-texture surface AddRef/Release retain the device and swapchain/texture storage on public zero/nonzero edges; a held surface keeps its container alive.
Public chain AddRef from zero reacquires one parent reference; repeated zero Release returns zero while physical backing storage survives.

documentation.evidence: Additional chains use the presentation multisample type and a quality index within advertised bounds; multisampling requires DISCARD.
